docs.title: Survivatorium Player's Guide
docs.text: Welcome to the official player guide for Survivatorium, a DayZ server running on the DeerIsle map with extensive modding for an enhanced survival experience.

docs.title: Server Rules (Summary)
docs.text:
• KOS allowed
  • No combat logging
  • Maximum 2 bases per group
  • No grief raiding
  • 500m build restriction from military areas

docs.title: Currency
docs.text: The server uses Hryvnia as the primary currency. Earn money through: - Completing quests - Selling items at traders - Player-to-player trading

docs.title: Getting Help

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Welcome to Survivatorium on DeerIsle. This guide covers everything you need to know for your first steps on the server.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Server Rules
  • Required Mods
  • First Spawn
  • The HUD
  • Your First Steps
  • Essential Keybinds

docs.title: General Conduct
docs.text:
• 1.1 No insults, discrimination, extremist, or racist statements - immediate ban
  • 1.2 Staff decisions are final; appeal via Discord tickets only
  • 1.3 No toxic behavior or excessive provocation in chat/voice
  • 1.4 No cheats, scripts, or third-party programs - permanent ban

docs.title: DeerIsle Questing
docs.text:
• 2.1 No exit-camping keycard vaults (KMUC, Temple, Crypt) for longer than 15 minutes
  • 2.2 No trapping players inside vaults using locks or buildables
  • 2.3 Do not block keycard readers with vehicles or items

docs.title: Base Building
docs.text:
• 3.1 No building within 500m of Military areas, Hospitals, Quest Entrances, or Mount Sage
  • 3.2 Bases must be realistic - no floating/sky bases
  • 3.3 Do not block public roads, bridges, or water wells
  • 3.4 Maximum 2 bases per faction/group

docs.title: Combat & Raiding
docs.text:
• 4.1 100% KOS map - there are no safezones
  • 4.2 No Combat Logging - wait 5 minutes after any engagement before logging out
  • 4.3 No Grief Raiding - take what you need, don't destroy bases out of spite
  • 4.4 No wall-glitching, emote-peeking, or body-stacking to bypass defenses

docs.title: Required Mods
docs.text: The server uses a carefully curated modpack to enhance the survival experience. You can find all the required mods in our Steam Workshop collection.

docs.title: Core Features
docs.text:
• DayZ Expansion: Overhauls many core mechanics, including the quest system, market, and territories.
  • BaseBuildingPlus: Provides extensive options for constructing your perfect base.
  • Custom Survival Mechanics: Enhanced medical, radiation, and skill systems to deepen the survival experience.

docs.title: Gameplay Enhancements
docs.text:
• KeyRooms & Hacked Crates: High-risk, high-reward loot locations scattered across the map.
  • Patrol Helicopters: Dynamic AI threats that patrol the skies.
  • Advanced Stamina: A reworked stamina system where your loadout weight and the terrain significantly impact your movement.
  • Breaching Charges: Specialized explosives used for raiding enemy bases.

docs.title: Weapons & Gear
docs.text:
• Tactical Flava & Forward Operator Gear: A massive arsenal of high-quality firearms, attachments, and tactical clothing.
  • Real-World Ammo & Ballistics: Authentic ammunition types and realistic ballistic trajectories.
  • MMG Storage: Visually distinct and high-capacity storage solutions for your base.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Subscribe to the Survivatorium mod collection on the Steam Workshop.
  2. Launch DayZ and let the launcher download all required mods.
  3. Join the server via the server browser or direct connect.

docs.title: First Spawn
docs.text:
When you first wake up on the shores of DeerIsle:

  1. Orientation Quest - You'll receive an automatic quest directing you to find the main Quest Board.
  2. Start Screen Flow - You will go through the Terje Start Screen pages (rules, name/face, skills, loadout, and map respawn selection).
  3. Starting Loadout - You can spawn with a starter loadout. Available options include a standard civilian kit, a larger custom loadout option, and conditional loadouts (for example, skill-gated or admin-only).
  4. Location - Default respawn is DeerIsle random coastal/inland spawn points, with extra options such as sleeping bag or deathpoint respawn when available.

docs.title: Spawn Areas
docs.text: DeerIsle has multiple spawn points along the coast. Common starting locations include: - Coastal towns - Near the main roads - Close to water sources

docs.title: The HUD
docs.text: The server features an enhanced HUD to help you monitor your vital stats:

docs.title: Core Indicators
docs.text:
• Health & Blood - Keep an eye on your overall condition.
  • White Stamina Bar - Your short-burst vanilla stamina (for sprinting, melee bursts, climbing, and fast movement).
  • Yellow Stamina Bar - Your long-term Inedia stamina pool, affected by weight, terrain, slope, and heat.
  • Hunger & Thirst - Essential survival indicators. Don't let these drop too low!
  • Temperature - Monitor your body heat to avoid freezing or overheating.

docs.title: Specialized Indicators
docs.text:
• Radiation Warning - A distinct warning will appear when you enter irradiated zones. Make sure you have the proper protective gear!
  • Skill Progress - Notifications will pop up as you level up your various survival skills.
  • Mind Icon (Terje Medicine) - Tracks mental state. Low mind can trigger severe penalties and dangerous behavior.
  • Sleep Icon (Terje Medicine) - Tracks fatigue from the Terje sleep system.
  • Reputation (right side) - Your progression currency for unlocking stronger trader access.

docs.title: Advanced Stamina
docs.text: The stamina system is heavily influenced by your gear: - Weight Matters: Running heavy is still punishing, but your current server settings are tuned to be more forgiving than default Inedia values. - Terrain Impact: Running uphill, through tall grass/forest, sand, and especially water drains your yellow stamina much faster than moving on roads.

docs.title: Step 1: Find Water and Food
docs.text:
• Look for water pumps in towns.
  • Search residential houses and greenhouses for canned food or fresh produce.
  • If you find a knife, you can hunt small animals or chickens for meat.

docs.title: Step 2: Arm Yourself
docs.text:
• Check houses and sheds for basic melee weapons like pipes, bats, or axes.
  • You might find a basic civilian firearm, but ammunition will be scarce early on.
  • Avoid military areas until you have a reliable weapon and some medical supplies.

docs.title: Step 3: Locate the Quest Board
docs.text: The Quest Board is your central hub for progression. Here you can: - Accept new quests. - Progress through various storylines. - Earn Hryvnia to spend at the market.

docs.title: Step 4: Complete the Orientation Quest
docs.text:
• Follow the marker to the Quest Board.
  • Interact with the board to complete your first quest and claim your reward.
  • Pick up your next assignment to continue your journey.

docs.title: Essential Keybinds
docs.text:
Action Default Key Inventory TAB Interact F Crafting Menu F9 Voice Chat CAPSLOCK

Note: Check your keybindings in the options menu to customize your controls, especially for modded features like the quest log or market interface.

docs.title: Inventory Management (Quality of Life)
docs.text: To make surviving a little less tedious, the server includes several Quality of Life (QoL) mods to help you manage your gear:

docs.title: Better Inspect
docs.text: Never guess which magazine fits your gun again! - How it works: Hover over an item in your inventory and press B (default key). - Color Coding: Items of the exact same type will highlight in Orange. Items that are compatible (like the correct ammo or attachments for a weapon) will highlight in Yellow.

docs.title: Hover Loot
docs.text: Quickly grab loot off the ground or dump unwanted items without dragging and dropping. - Quick Loot: Hover over an item on the ground and hold H to instantly move it to your inventory. - Quick Drop: Hover over an item in your inventory and press SHIFT + H to instantly drop it on the ground. - Quick Store: Hover over an item in your inventory and hold H to move it into the first available storage container on the ground (like a tent or barrel).

docs.title: Tips for New Players
docs.text:
1. Trust no one - The map is 100% KOS (Kill on Sight). Always be on your guard.
  2. Stay hydrated - Clean water is essential. Purify water from ponds or streams if you can't find a well.
  3. Travel light - Don't hoard every item you find. Manage your weight to maintain your stamina and mobility.
  4. Learn the map - Knowing the layout of DeerIsle, including key landmarks and military zones, will save your life.
  5. Use the market - Sell excess loot to traders to earn Hryvnia for the gear you actually need.
  6. Join a group - Survival is easier with friends. You can form a group and claim a territory together.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Ready to learn more? Check out: - Base Building - Establish your foothold - Quests & Traders - Start earning currency - Survival Systems - Master the elements

docs.title: Base Building
docs.text: Learn how to establish and defend your base on Survivatorium. We use a combination of BaseBuildingPlus and the Expansion territory system to give you the freedom to build the ultimate stronghold.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Territory System
  • Crafting & Workbenches
  • BaseBuildingPlus
  • Code Locks
  • Raiding Mechanics
  • Base Defense Tips
  • Building Rules

docs.title: Territory System
docs.text: Before you can start building your fortress, you need to claim the land. Territories define your safe zone and control who is allowed to build within your area.

docs.title: Territory Limits
docs.text:
• Territory Radius: 60 meters
  • Max Members: 5 players per territory
  • Max Territories: 1 per player

docs.title: Creating a Territory
docs.text:
1. Craft or find a Territory Flag Kit.
  2. Place the flag where you want the center of your base to be.
  3. Raise the flag and name your territory.
  4. Invite your friends via the territory menu.

docs.title: Territory Management
docs.text:
• Inviting Members: Your friends must be within the 150m radius to accept your invite (invite range is separate from territory size).
  • Permissions: Only territory members can build or dismantle structures within the radius.
  • Important: Code locks do NOT automatically authenticate territory members. You still need to share your door codes with your group!

docs.title: Crafting & Workbenches
docs.text: Survivatorium features an advanced crafting system that goes beyond the vanilla DayZ mechanics.

docs.title: The Crafting Menu (F9)
docs.text: Press F9 to open the custom crafting menu. This is your starting point for advanced survival. From here, you can craft essential tools and your first Workbench.

docs.title: The Workbench
docs.text: Once you've crafted and placed a Workbench, you unlock a whole new tier of recipes. - Base Building Parts: Craft the specialized components needed for BaseBuildingPlus structures. - Ammunition: Press your own ammo to keep your weapons fed. - Upgrades: The Workbench can be upgraded to unlock even more advanced recipes. - Consumables: Keep an eye out for consumable items that might be required for high-tier crafting.

docs.title: BaseBuildingPlus
docs.text: BaseBuildingPlus (BBP) gives you the tools to build everything from a simple wooden shack to a massive concrete bunker.

docs.title: Getting Started with BBP
docs.text: Once you have your Workbench set up and your BBP parts crafted, you'll need the right tools: - Hammer or Sledgehammer - Nails - Planks, Logs, or Metal Plates (depending on the tier)

docs.title: Building Tiers
docs.text:
• Wood: The easiest to gather, but the weakest against explosives.
  • Concrete: Highly durable, requires cement and a concrete mixer.
  • Metal: The ultimate protection, requiring sheet metal and specialized tools.

docs.title: Structure Types
docs.text:
• Foundations & Floors: Establish a flat surface on uneven terrain.
  • Walls & Half-Walls: Create your perimeter and internal rooms.
  • Doors & Gates: Secure your entrances.
  • Defenses: Sandbags, barbed wire, and watchtowers to repel attackers.

docs.title: Code Locks
docs.text: Code locks are essential for securing your base doors and high-tier storage containers.

docs.title: Setting Up Code Locks
docs.text:
1. Attach the code lock to a compatible door, gate, or storage container.
  2. Set your 4-digit PIN.
  3. Remember your code! Lost codes cannot be recovered by admins.
  4. Share the code with your trusted group members.

docs.title: Security Tips
docs.text:
• Use different codes for your outer gates and inner loot rooms.
  • Change your codes periodically if you suspect someone might have learned them.
  • Avoid obvious codes like 1234 or 0000.

docs.title: Raiding Mechanics
docs.text: Survivatorium is a dangerous place. Bases can be raided 24/7, meaning you must always be prepared to defend your loot.

docs.title: Breaching Charges
docs.text: Standard melee tools won't get you through a reinforced BBP wall. To raid a base, you will need Breaching Charges. - Finding Charges: Breaching charges and their components are rare and highly sought after. Look for them in high-tier military zones, KeyRooms, or Airdrops. - Planting: Attach the charge to the door or wall you want to destroy. - Detonation: Stand back! The explosion will destroy the structure, granting you access to the base.

docs.title: Other Raiding Tools
docs.text:
While walls require explosives, some smaller obstacles can be bypassed with the right tools: - Safes & Containers: Can sometimes be cracked open using a Propane Torch, though it takes a significant amount of time and fuel. - Barbed Wire: Can be cut using Bolt Cutters.

Note: Standard locks on walls and fences cannot be picked or sawed off. You must blow the door off its hinges!

docs.title: Layer Your Defense
docs.text:
1. Outer Perimeter: Use barbed wire and natural obstacles to slow down attackers.
  2. Multiple Doors: Don't rely on a single gate. Build "airlocks" with multiple locked doors to force raiders to use more explosives.
  3. Mix Materials: Upgrade your most vulnerable walls to concrete or metal as soon as possible.

docs.title: Smart Storage
docs.text:
• Don't keep all your high-tier loot in one room.
  • Use secure containers (like safes or MMG lockers) and attach code locks to them for an extra layer of security.

docs.title: Building Rules
docs.text:
To keep the server fair and performant, please adhere to the following rules: - No building within 500m of Military areas, Hospitals, Quest Entrances, or Mount Sage. - Bases must be realistic. No floating or "sky" bases. - Do not block public roads, bridges, or water wells. - Maximum 2 bases per faction/group. - No Grief Raiding: Take what you need, but do not destroy a base purely out of spite.

Violating these rules may result in your base being deleted by the admin team.

docs.title: Quests & Traders
docs.text: Master the quest system and economy to earn Hryvnia and progress on Survivatorium.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Currency
  • Quest System
  • Questlines
  • The Market
  • Trading Tips

docs.title: Hryvnia
docs.text: The server uses Hryvnia as the primary currency. You'll need it to buy gear, vehicles, and supplies from the traders.

docs.title: Earning Hryvnia
docs.text:
• Quest Rewards: Completing quests is the most reliable way to earn money.
  • Selling Items: Scavenge the wasteland and sell valuable loot to the traders.
  • Player Trading: Sell rare items directly to other players.
  • Airdrops: High-risk airdrops often contain large stacks of cash.

docs.title: Starting Money
docs.text: New players receive a small starting stipend of Hryvnia upon completing their initial orientation.

docs.title: Quest Board
docs.text: The Quest Board is your central hub for finding work. Located in the main settlement area, it offers a variety of contracts for mercenaries and survivors alike.

docs.title: Quest Interface
docs.text: When you open a quest, you'll see: - Description: The backstory and context for your mission. - Objective: Exactly what you need to do (e.g., travel to a location, kill a target, deliver an item). - Rewards: The Hryvnia, items, and Reputation you will earn upon completion.

docs.title: Quest Types
docs.text:
• Travel: Scout out a specific location.
  • Delivery: Transport sensitive items to an NPC.
  • Collection: Gather specific supplies (like medical gear or food) and turn them in.
  • Hunt: Track down and eliminate specific wildlife.
  • Elimination: Clear out infected or hostile AI mercenaries.
  • Escort: Protect VIPs as they move through dangerous territory.

docs.title: Quest Mechanics
docs.text:
• Chains: Many quests are part of a larger storyline. Completing one will unlock the next.
  • Reputation: High-tier, lucrative quests require you to build up your Reputation first.
  • Group Quests: Some of the harder missions are best tackled with a squad.

docs.title: Questlines
docs.text: There are several major storylines and contract types available on the server. Here are a few you can expect to encounter:

docs.title: Orientation
docs.text: Your first task upon waking up on DeerIsle. It will guide you to the Quest Board and introduce you to the basics of survival.

docs.title: Medical Support
docs.text: Contact: STAG Medical Chief Officer Peters The medical staff is always in need of supplies and capable hands. You'll start with basic medic training and progress to dangerous supply runs into infected territory.

docs.title: Hunting Contracts
docs.text: The local populace needs food, and the wildlife needs culling. You can pick up contracts to hunt everything from chickens and pigs to dangerous predators like wolves and bears. The more dangerous the prey, the higher the payout.

docs.title: Threat Intelligence
docs.text: Contact: STAG Threat Intelligence Officer Harris For the combat-oriented survivor. These missions involve scouting enemy AI camps, intercepting black site communications, and engaging in heavy firefights.

docs.title: Mopping Up & Field Validation
docs.text: Prove your worth by clearing out designated zones of infected and hostile mercenaries. These quests scale in difficulty and are a great way to test your combat skills.

docs.title: VIP Escort
docs.text: High-value targets need to be moved across the island. You'll be tasked with protecting them from ambushes as they travel to extraction points like the Power Plant or Paris Island.

docs.title: Treasure Hunts
docs.text: Follow cryptic clues to find hidden stashes of valuable loot scattered across the map.

docs.title: The Market
docs.text: The Market is where you'll spend your hard-earned Hryvnia. Traders are set up in safe zones to buy and sell goods.

docs.title: What You Can Buy & Sell
docs.text:
• Weapons & Ammo: Everything from basic civilian rifles to advanced military hardware, plus the ammunition and magazines to keep them firing.
  • Attachments: Optics, suppressors, grips, and more to customize your firearms.
  • Clothing & Armor: Basic survival gear, high-end tactical clothing (like FOG gear), helmets, and plate carriers.
  • Medical Supplies: Bandages, blood bags, specialized injectors, and radiation medication.
  • Base Building: Tools, nails, and materials to construct your stronghold.
  • Vehicles: Cars, boats, and helicopters (if you have the cash!).
  • Miscellaneous & Collectibles: Keep an eye out for rare, random items scattered across the world. Some of these oddities can fetch a high price at the right trader!

docs.title: Trading Tips
docs.text:
• Condition Matters: Traders will pay less for damaged goods. Repair your weapons and clothing before selling them if possible.
  • Supply and Demand: Keep an eye on what the traders need. Some items might fetch a premium.
  • Save for the Good Stuff: Don't blow all your money on basic gear. Save up for high-tier weapons, vehicles, or base building supplies that are hard to find in the wild.

docs.title: Combat & Weapons
docs.text: Master the arsenal of Survivatorium. With an expanded selection of firearms, realistic ballistics, and deadly AI threats, you'll need to know your weapons to survive.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• The Arsenal
  • Weapon Customization
  • Real-World Ammo & Ballistics
  • Reputation & Gear Access
  • AI Threats
  • Combat Tips

docs.title: The Arsenal
docs.text: Survivatorium features a massive variety of firearms, blending vanilla DayZ weapons with high-quality additions from the Tactical Flava and DayZ Expansion mods.

docs.title: Weapon Categories
docs.text:
• Sidearms: From basic Makarovs to high-capacity FN Five-seveNs and Desert Eagles. Perfect for backup or dealing with infected.
  • Submachine Guns: MP5s, P90s, and MP7s. Excellent for close-quarters combat and clearing buildings.
  • Assault Rifles: The backbone of any survivor's loadout. Choose from the reliable AK platform, versatile M4s, heavy-hitting SCARs, and more.
  • Sniper & Marksman Rifles: For those who prefer to engage from a distance. Includes classic bolt-actions like the Mosin and modern DMRs like the M110.
  • Shotguns: Devastating at close range. Ranging from double-barrel hunting shotguns to tactical semi-automatics like the Benelli M4.
  • Heavy Weapons: For when you absolutely need to destroy a target (or a base). Includes RPGs, LAWs, and grenade launchers.

docs.title: Weapon Customization
docs.text: A stock rifle is just the beginning. You can customize your firearms to suit your playstyle using a wide array of attachments.

docs.title: Optics
docs.text: Choose the right sight for the job: - Red Dots & Holographics: Fast target acquisition for close-to-medium range (e.g., EOTech, M68). - Magnified Optics: Versatile scopes for medium engagements (e.g., ACOG, HAMR). - Sniper Scopes: High-magnification optics for extreme long-range precision. - Night Vision: Specialized scopes for operating in the dark.

docs.title: Suppressors & Muzzles
docs.text:
• Suppressors: Reduce your acoustic signature to avoid drawing unwanted attention from infected or other players.
  • Compensators: Help manage recoil for faster follow-up shots.

docs.title: Furniture
docs.text: Upgrade your weapon's handling and ergonomics by swapping out handguards, buttstocks, and pistol grips. Many Tactical Flava weapons offer extensive modularity, allowing you to build your perfect rifle.

docs.title: Real-World Ammo & Ballistics
docs.text: Survivatorium uses the Real-World Ammo & Ballistics mod, which significantly changes how firearms behave compared to vanilla DayZ.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Authentic Calibers: Weapons use their real-world ammunition types. Make sure you're loading the correct caliber!
  • Realistic Trajectories: Bullets experience realistic drop and wind drift over distance. You will need to learn how to zero your optics and compensate for bullet drop.
  • Penetration & Damage: Different calibers have different penetration values. A 5.56x45mm round will behave very differently against body armor than a 7.62x51mm round.
  • Armor Matters: High-tier plate carriers and helmets will save your life against smaller calibers, but heavy sniper rounds or armor-piercing ammunition can still punch through.

docs.title: Reputation & Gear Access
docs.text: Your standing on the server directly impacts the gear you can acquire.

docs.title: The Reputation System
docs.text: As you complete quests, hunt dangerous animals, and eliminate hostile AI, you will earn Reputation. - Death Penalty: Dying will cost you a significant amount of Reputation, so play carefully!

docs.title: Unlocking the Good Stuff
docs.text: Traders won't sell their best gear to just anyone. - Basic Gear: Common tools, civilian clothing, and low-tier weapons are available to everyone. - Advanced Gear: As your Reputation grows, you'll unlock access to military-grade firearms, high-end optics, and heavy armor. - Top-Tier Loot: The most exotic and devastating weapons require a very high Reputation score to purchase.

docs.title: AI Threats
docs.text: You aren't just fighting other players and infected. DeerIsle is populated by dangerous AI factions.

docs.title: Hostile Mercenaries
docs.text: Heavily armed AI patrols guard key military installations and high-value loot zones. They use squad tactics, take cover, and will engage you on sight.

docs.title: Patrol Helicopters
docs.text: Keep an eye on the sky. Heavily armed patrol helicopters occasionally sweep the island. If they spot you, they will open fire with devastating weaponry. Taking one down yields incredible rewards, but it requires heavy firepower and coordination.

docs.title: Trophies of War (Dogtags)
docs.text: When you engage in PvP and emerge victorious, you can claim a trophy to prove your skills. - Collecting Dogtags: When you kill another player, you can loot their Dogtag from their body. - Secure Containers: You can store these dogtags safely in specialized secure containers to ensure you don't lose your hard-earned trophies if you are killed on your way back to base.

docs.title: Combat Tips
docs.text:
1. Check Your Zero: Always know what distance your optic is zeroed to before taking a shot.
  2. Manage Your Stamina: Don't drain your stamina right before a firefight. You need it to hold your breath for steady aiming.
  3. Use Cover: The AI is deadly accurate. Never stand in the open during a firefight.
  4. Bring Medical Supplies: Always carry bandages, blood bags, and morphine. A single bullet can cause heavy bleeding or unconsciousness.
  5. Know When to Run: If you're outgunned or pinned down by a patrol helicopter, sometimes the best tactic is to retreat and survive.

docs.title: Survival Systems
docs.text: Surviving on DeerIsle requires more than just a loaded gun. You must manage your physical condition, treat complex injuries, and navigate hazardous environments.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Advanced Stamina
  • Character Skills
  • Advanced Medicine
  • Radiation Zones

docs.title: Advanced Stamina
docs.text: Survivatorium features a realistic stamina system that forces you to think carefully about your loadout and your route.

docs.title: Two Stamina Bars (Important)
docs.text:
• White bar: Short-burst vanilla stamina for immediate actions.
  • Yellow bar: Inedia general stamina (long-term endurance).

On this server, Inedia stamina is active, while Inedia's own sleep stamina is disabled. Your sleep/fatigue gameplay comes from the Terje medicine system instead.

docs.title: Weight Matters
docs.text: The more gear you carry, the slower you will move and the faster your stamina will drain. - Light Load: Optimal for long-distance travel and combat mobility. - Heavy Load: You will experience noticeable slowdowns, especially once you move into very high carry weight. - Overloaded: The harsh movement penalties begin much later than vanilla-style hardcore setups, but if you push too far you can still be forced into walking and eventually movement lock.

docs.title: Terrain & Slopes
docs.text: Your environment directly impacts your energy levels: - Surfaces: Running on paved roads is highly efficient. Running through tall grass, deep snow, or wading through water will exhaust you quickly. - Slopes: Sprinting up a steep hill will drain your stamina in seconds. Plan your routes to avoid steep inclines if you are heavily geared.

docs.title: How This Server Is Tuned
docs.text:
• More forgiving than default Inedia: Sprint/jog drain is reduced compared to stock wiki values, so players can stay active longer in PvP and movement-heavy fights.
  • Low/Critical thresholds: Debuffs begin at roughly low yellow stamina, and become severe at critical yellow stamina.
  • Heat still matters: Overheating increases stamina consumption, so temperature management is still part of movement planning.

docs.title: Energy Drinks
docs.text: Keep an eye out for energy drinks (like MadBull or Pipsi). Consuming them will give you a temporary boost to your stamina recovery, which can be a lifesaver during a long trek or a firefight.

docs.title: The Metro Watch
docs.text: A true survivor needs to keep track of time and their environment. The Metro Watch is a highly sought-after piece of gear that provides crucial information at a glance. - Time & Date: Keep track of daylight hours so you aren't caught out in the dark. - Environmental Data: Some models can help you monitor your surroundings, making it an invaluable tool for navigating the harsh weather of DeerIsle.

docs.title: Character Skills
docs.text: As you survive and perform actions in the world, your character will learn and grow.

docs.title: Skill Progression
docs.text: You gain experience simply by playing the game. - Athletics & Strength: Running, jumping, and carrying gear will slowly improve your physical capabilities. - Metabolism & Immunity: Eating, drinking, and fighting off diseases will make your body more resilient. - Survival & Hunting: Starting fires, skinning animals, and fishing will make you a master of the wilderness. - Medicine: Treating wounds and using medical supplies will make your treatments more effective.

docs.title: Perks & Skill Books
docs.text:
As you level up your skills, you will unlock powerful perks that grant permanent bonuses, such as reduced weapon sway, better disease resistance, or the ability to carry more weight. You can also find Skill Books scattered across the world. Reading these will grant you a burst of experience in a specific skill tree.

Note: Your skills are persistent. You do not lose your hard-earned experience when you die!

docs.title: Advanced Medicine
docs.text: A simple bandage won't fix everything anymore. The medical system is deep and requires specific treatments for specific injuries.

docs.title: Types of Injuries
docs.text:
• Light Bleeds: Minor cuts and scrapes. Can be treated with standard bandages or rags.
  • Heavy Bleeds & Deep Wounds: Caused by severe trauma. These require more advanced medical attention, sometimes even field surgery, before they can be properly bandaged.
  • Bullet Wounds: If you take a bullet, it might stay in your body. You will need a surgical kit to extract the bullet before the wound can fully heal.
  • Fractures: Falling from heights or taking heavy blunt damage can break your bones. You will need a splint and painkillers to keep moving.

docs.title: Diseases & Infections
docs.text:
• Wound Infection: Always use disinfected bandages! Using dirty rags will lead to sepsis, which requires strong antibiotics to cure.
  • Zombie Virus: Getting hit by infected carries a risk of contracting the zombie virus. Keep antiviral medication on hand.
  • Food Poisoning: Eating raw meat or drinking dirty water will make you violently ill. Charcoal tablets are your best friend.

docs.title: Radiation Zones
docs.text: Certain high-value military areas and key locations on DeerIsle are highly irradiated. Entering these zones unprepared is a death sentence.

docs.title: The Geiger Counter
docs.text: Always carry a Geiger counter when exploring unknown territory. It will click and warn you when radiation levels are rising.

docs.title: Protection
docs.text: To survive in a radiation zone, you need specialized gear: - NBC Suits: A full NBC suit (hood, jacket, pants, boots, and gloves) combined with a gas mask and filter will protect you from environmental radiation. - Filters: Gas mask filters degrade over time while in a radiation zone. Always bring spares!

docs.title: Treatment
docs.text: If you absorb too much radiation, you will develop acute radiation sickness. This causes vomiting, blood loss, and eventually death. You must use specialized anti-radiation medication (like Rad-X or Potassium Iodide) to purge the radiation from your system.

docs.title: Vehicles
docs.text: DeerIsle is a massive map. Walking everywhere will drain your stamina and leave you vulnerable. Finding, repairing, and securing a vehicle is a major milestone in your survival journey.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Vehicle Types
  • Keys & Locks
  • Lockpicking
  • Towing
  • Maintenance
  • Helicopters
  • Boats

docs.title: Vehicle Types
docs.text: Survivatorium offers a variety of vehicles to suit your needs, from simple transport to heavy military hardware.

docs.title: Cars & Trucks
docs.text:
• Civilian Vehicles: Standard cars and off-roaders (like the UAZ) are great for getting around quickly.
  • Transport: Buses and cargo trucks are perfect for moving large groups or hauling base-building supplies.
  • Military: Armored vehicles like the Vodnik offer superior protection but are rare and expensive to maintain.

docs.title: Boats
docs.text: With DeerIsle's extensive waterways and islands, boats are incredibly useful. - Zodiacs: Fast, light, and easy to hide. - Utility Boats: Better for transporting gear and small groups.

docs.title: Helicopters
docs.text: The ultimate flex. Helicopters allow you to bypass the dangerous roads entirely, but they are difficult to fly and expensive to maintain. - Light Choppers: The MH-6 Little Bird is fast and agile. - Heavy Transport: The Merlin and Huey can carry your whole squad and a massive amount of loot.

docs.title: Keys & Locks
docs.text: A vehicle without a key is just a temporary ride. To truly own a vehicle, you need to secure it.

docs.title: How Keys Work
docs.text:
• Starting the Engine: You must have the paired key in your inventory to start the vehicle.
  • Locking: You can lock the vehicle to prevent others from accessing the inventory or getting in. Note: All doors must be attached to fully secure the vehicle!

docs.title: Getting Keys
docs.text:
• Finding Them: Sometimes you'll get lucky and find a vehicle that spawned with its key inside.
  • Buying Them: Traders sell blank keys and master keys.
  • Copying: You can use a Master Key to create a duplicate of an existing key, which is essential for sharing access with your group.

docs.title: Lockpicking
docs.text: Found a locked vehicle you want to steal? You'll need a Lockpick and a lot of patience.

docs.title: The Process
docs.text:
1. Approach the locked vehicle with a Lockpick in your hands.
  2. Start the lockpicking action.
  3. Wait: Lockpicking takes a significant amount of time, leaving you completely exposed.
  4. Chance of Success: It is not guaranteed! You might fail, and every attempt will damage your lockpick.

docs.title: Lock Complexity
docs.text: Not all locks are created equal. A simple Zodiac boat is relatively easy to pick, while a military Vodnik or a heavy transport helicopter has complex security systems that will test your patience and your supply of lockpicks.

docs.title: Towing
docs.text: Found a broken-down car but don't have the parts to fix it on the spot? Tow it home!

docs.title: How to Tow
docs.text:
1. Position a working vehicle in front of the broken one.
  2. Access the interaction menu on the working vehicle and select the tow option.
  3. Attach the tow cable to the rear vehicle.

docs.title: Towing Tips
docs.text:
• The towing vehicle needs a strong engine to pull the extra weight.
  • The towed vehicle has no steering control, so take your turns wide and drive carefully!
  • Always detach the towed vehicle before logging off or parking for the night.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text: Vehicles require constant upkeep. If you neglect them, they will leave you stranded.

docs.title: Essential Parts
docs.text:
• Cars: Spark Plug (or Glow Plug for diesel), Car Battery, Radiator (filled with water!), and four intact tires.
  • Helicopters: Helicopter Battery, Igniter Plug, Hydraulic Hoses, and a working Tail Rotor.
  • Boats: Spark Plug and fuel.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
• Won't Start: Check the battery and spark plug. Make sure you have fuel!
  • Overheating: Your radiator is either ruined or empty. Stop immediately and add water, or you will destroy the engine.
  • Pulling to One Side: You have a ruined tire. Use a Tire Repair Kit or find a replacement.

docs.title: Helicopters: A Warning
docs.text: Flying a helicopter is dangerous. - Pre-Flight Check: Always check your fuel, battery, and hydraulic hoses before taking off. - Tail Rotors: The tail rotor is fragile. If it takes damage from gunfire or a bad landing, you will lose control and spin out of the sky. - Crashes: Helicopter crashes are catastrophic and will result in a massive explosion, destroying the vehicle and killing everyone inside. Practice in a safe area before taking your squad on a joyride!

docs.title: KeyRooms & Airdrops
docs.text: If you want the best gear on DeerIsle, you can't just scavenge through empty houses. You need to take risks. KeyRooms and Airdrops offer the highest tier loot, but they are highly contested.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• KeyRooms
  • Finding Keys
  • KeyRoom Loot
  • Airdrops
  • Airdrop Loot

docs.title: KeyRooms
docs.text: Scattered across the map are secure rooms and vaults locked behind heavy doors. To get inside, you need the right key.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Find a Key: Keys and keycards are rare drops found on infected, in military zones, or sometimes sold by specialized traders.
  2. Locate the Room: You'll need to explore to find where these keys belong. Some are hidden in plain sight in cities, while others are buried deep in military bunkers.
  3. Unlock: Approach the locked door or keypad with the key in your hand to unlock it.
  4. Loot Fast: Grab what you can. The door will automatically lock behind you after a set time, and you don't want to be trapped inside!

Warning: Do not exit-camp keycard vaults (like the KMUC, Temple, or Crypt) for longer than 15 minutes, and never trap players inside vaults using locks or buildables. This violates server rules.

docs.title: Finding Keys
docs.text: Keys are color-coded to give you a hint about where they might be used: - Grey Keys: Typically unlock secure rooms located within major Cities. - Green Keys: Usually open stashes hidden in Camps and rural areas. - (There are many more key types and colors to discover as you explore the island!)

docs.title: KeyRoom Loot
docs.text: The risk is worth the reward. KeyRooms contain curated loot that is significantly better than what you'll find lying around in the open.

docs.title: What to Expect
docs.text:
• Weapons: Depending on the room, you might find anything from reliable starter submachine guns to devastating, high-tier military sniper rifles.
  • Medical Supplies: Secure medical rooms contain advanced trauma kits, blood bags, and crucial anti-radiation medication.
  • Tactical Gear: You can find high-end clothing and armor, including advanced Crye G3 suits, heavy plate carriers, and specialized arctic gear for surviving the cold.

docs.title: Airdrops
docs.text: Airdrops are dynamic, server-wide events that deliver massive crates of high-value loot to random locations.

docs.title: Mechanics
docs.text:
• The Alert: A server-wide notification will warn all players when an airdrop is incoming.
  • The Drop: Look to the sky for the transport plane. It will drop a large crate via parachute. Once it lands, a smoke flare will mark the exact location.
  • The Danger: Airdrops are a beacon for every geared player on the server. Approach with extreme caution, as they are highly contested PvP hotspots.

docs.title: Airdrop Loot
docs.text: If you manage to secure an airdrop and survive, you will be heavily rewarded. The crates contain exclusive items that are incredibly difficult to find anywhere else.

docs.title: The Haul
docs.text:
• Base Building: Rare materials, heavy tools, and sometimes even breaching charges or explosives.
  • Advanced Weaponry: Fully kitted assault rifles, rare attachments, and heavy machine guns.
  • Top-Tier Armor: The best helmets and plate carriers available.
  • Cash: Large stacks of Hryvnia to fund your next expedition.

Tip: Don't get greedy. Grab the most valuable items and get out before another squad arrives to contest the drop!

docs.title: Advanced Topics
docs.text: Once you've mastered the basics of survival, it's time to look at the deeper mechanics of Survivatorium. This guide covers the Reputation system, Player-to-Player trading, and advanced storage solutions.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Reputation System
  • Player-to-Player (P2P) Market
  • Personal Storage

docs.title: Reputation System
docs.text: Your Reputation is a measure of your standing on the server. It is a crucial metric that dictates what you can buy and what missions you can undertake.

docs.title: Earning Reputation
docs.text:
• Completing Quests: The primary and most reliable way to earn Reputation. Higher-tier quests reward more points.
  • Killing Threats: Eliminating infected, dangerous wildlife, and hostile AI mercenaries will slowly build your standing.
  • Events: Participating in server events or securing airdrops can also boost your Reputation.

docs.title: Losing Reputation
docs.text:
• Death: Dying incurs a massive Reputation penalty. This makes survival absolutely crucial for progression. If you die frequently, you will find yourself locked out of high-tier gear.
  • Failing Quests: Some quests may penalize you for failure or abandonment.

docs.title: Reputation Benefits
docs.text:
• Quest Unlocks: Many advanced questlines (like Threat Intelligence or Field Validation) require a minimum Reputation score before the NPC will even speak to you.
  • Trader Access: Traders reserve their best weapons, armor, and vehicles for reputable players. If your Reputation is too low, you won't be able to purchase high-end military gear.

docs.title: Player-to-Player (P2P) Market
docs.text: The P2P Market allows players to trade items directly with each other, bypassing the NPC traders and setting their own prices.

docs.title: How to Use the P2P Market
docs.text:
1. Access the Market: Locate a P2P Market terminal (often found in safe zones or major trader hubs).
  2. List an Item: Select an item from your inventory, set your asking price in Hryvnia, and list it on the market.
  3. Buy an Item: Browse the listings from other players. If you have enough Hryvnia, you can purchase the item instantly, even if the seller is offline.
  4. Collect Earnings: When your item sells, the Hryvnia is deposited into your account or can be collected from the market terminal.

docs.title: P2P Trading Tips
docs.text:
• Supply and Demand: Check the NPC trader prices before listing. If an item is rare or out of stock at the NPC, you can charge a premium.
  • Undercutting: To sell quickly, price your items slightly lower than the competition.
  • Bulk Sales: Selling items in bulk (e.g., stacks of ammo, building materials, or medical supplies) is often more attractive to buyers.

docs.title: Personal Storage
docs.text: Managing your loot is a critical part of survival. Survivatorium offers several advanced storage options beyond the standard DayZ tents and barrels.

docs.title: MMG Storage
docs.text:
The server uses the MMG Storage mod, which provides a variety of high-capacity, visually distinct storage containers to organize your base.

  • Gun Racks: Display and store your firearms efficiently.
  • Gear Stands: Store clothing, armor, and backpacks so they are ready to grab after a death.
  • Lockers & Crates: High-capacity storage for general items, building supplies, and medical gear.

docs.title: Secure Storage
docs.text:
• Code Locks: You can attach Code Locks to tents, barrels, and MMG storage containers to secure your loot from thieves. Even if someone breaches your base walls, they will still need to crack your containers.
  • Territory Protection: Items stored within your claimed territory are protected by your base's defenses, but remember that bases can be raided!

docs.title: Storage Limits
docs.text: • Be mindful of server performance. While there are no strict limits on the number of storage containers you can have, excessive hoarding in a single area can cause lag for you and your neighbors.
